properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar, north arrow, and real street labels (Illinois St, Georgia St, Louisiana St, Maryland St, Delaware St, 22nd St, Humboldt St, 23rd St), not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 9 real street-intersection control points fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py, fit as a least-squares affine transform. NOTE: an initial attempt also used the real, confirmed positions of the Sophie Maxwell Building and the UCSF Block 2 building as anchors, but they produced 50-60m of error against the street-only fit -- this diagram is dated Feb 26, 2020, predating UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as a life-science anchor tenant, so those two real buildings likely do not sit where this 2020 figure's own numbered blocks would place them (their own real parcels are used directly elsewhere in this dataset and were NOT re-derived from this diagram). The final transform here uses street intersections only. Residual error against those control points is roughly 8-24m. Traced polygons were additionally clipped against the real, confirmed Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels (and against Prequel Park's approximate geometry) so this speculative tracing never overrides real or better-sourced geometry. OVERLAP FIX 2026-09-14: Clipped against Station A (Block 15) -- Station A is a real, well-documented historic building with an approved reuse project, taking priority over this generic numbered block's speculative boundary. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: user-flagged pattern of blocks encroaching on real streets across the site (Block 3, Block 11, Block 12) led to rebuilding this whole block layer from scratch using proper GCP-based georeferencing (GDAL's gdaltransform with a thin-plate-spline transform, the same technique QGIS's Georeferencer uses) instead of patching individual curbs. Installed GDAL, computed 8 real street-intersection ground control points from OpenStreetMap data (Craig Lane x Maryland St, 22nd St x Maryland/Louisiana St, Humboldt St x Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane, 23rd St x Maryland/Georgia Lane), precisely located each in the source diagram (Figure 6.2.3) via programmatic black-pixel border detection cross-checked with visual ruler crops, and fit a TPS transform. Re-traced this block's own corner pixels the same way and ran them through the new transform. This corrected transform disagrees with the original 9-point affine transform by tens of meters in places -- e.g. it revealed the original trace had Blocks 3/4 shifted east into the excavation pit/street area, and Blocks 11/12 roughly 2x too deep -- and the new positions now land within real, distinct site features (buildings, graded lots) visible in satellite imagery rather than straddling roads. Known residual limitation: GCP street positions are centerline-based (matching OSM convention), while a block boundary should sit at the near curb, so any edge close to a GCP street can land a few meters into that street after transformation -- checked for and corrected on this block's street-facing edge(s) where applicable using this project's already-established grid bearing (356.5 deg) and, where available, an independently diagram-measured depth/width. Treat corrected vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (tighter than the original 8-24m transform, but still not survey-grade). RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (same day, third pass): the independent per-block TPS re-trace (see above) still measured each block's own 4 corners in isolation, which -- despite using the same transform -- left small (3-12m) spurious gaps or misalignments at boundaries the diagram actually draws as shared or tightly-spaced between adjacent blocks (caught after the user pointed out the diagram itself has ~zero wasted space and specifically that the PG&E switchyard polygon sits directly against Block 5 in the diagram, not ~60m away as this dataset had it). Re-measured EVERY block's corners in a single consistent pass using programmatic black-pixel border detection (long contiguous runs = real borders, filtered from text/dimension-arrow strokes by requiring the run to span nearly the full block height/width), cross-validated with fine-pixel-gridline crops, so that shared or consistently-measured boundaries between neighboring blocks now come from the same underlying pixel measurements rather than independent eyeball estimates. Batch-transformed through the same GDAL/TPS fit as before. This pass also corrected several block extents that were measured imprecisely in the prior pass (e.g. Block 5's real stepped/notched south edge, Block 11's true position -- it does NOT sit flush against Block 15, there is real Power Station Park open space between them). GCP CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (fourth pass): user flagged that Block 8/12 should touch Delaware Street with park space between them, and that Block 3/4's shapes looked off -- investigation found the root cause was a single mis-measured ground control point. The 'Delaware St x Humboldt St' GCP used for the whole site's TPS transform had been placed at pixel (2227, 986), which is actually deep inside Building 9's own footprint in the diagram, not on Delaware Street at all -- confirmed by comparing pixel spacing between the three Humboldt-row GCPs (Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane): Maryland-to-Georgia-Lane's pixel:real-world ratio implied Delaware should sit at roughly pixel x=2020, not 2227, and a direct color-transition scan at y=986 confirmed the real street gap is at x=1994-2035. Corrected the GCP to (2015, 986) (same real-world coordinate, just the right pixel) and re-ran the TPS transform for the whole site. This produced large corrections concentrated exactly where the user's complaint pointed -- Block 4 shifted 33-60m, Block 3's east corners ~28-33m, Block 8's east corners ~29-31m, Block 12's east corners ~26-27m -- while blocks far from the error (5, 15, 7, 11, PG&E) shifted well under 5m, consistent with a localized GCP error rather than a global transform problem. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source URL cited for this file (the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the D4D at default.sfplanning.org) is dead (404); the text above describes the final D4D (dated February 26, 2020), so source_doc_urls now points to potreropower_D4D_final.pdf, where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) with a scale bar (0-400 ft), a north arrow and the street labels listed above. The '~2023-24 arrival' of UCSF as anchor tenant, mentioned above, has no cited source; the dated source found is the UC Regents' September 2024 CEQA findings (Attachment 6), which state that in 2024 the City approved an assignment and assumption agreement under which UCSF assumes a portion of the developer's rights. The Sophie Maxwell / UCSF Block 2 anchor and clip steps are this project's own work, not a source claim. The height callouts and program statements in regulatory_context were corrected on the same date; the committed geometry was not changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (no design-review approval or construction start found; it is not in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list) and no Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows about 93% of its footprint within the much larger active lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln, about 15,900 sq m, recorded 2024-10-15). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see accuracy_caveat. Status 'planned': shown in the final D4D, and SocketSite's October 2020 schedule table lists Block 5 in Phase 3 (vertical development 2031-2034). Use 'mixed': residential, institutional, retail, office and limited PDR uses are permitted (D4D Table 3.1.1).'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (no design-review approval or construction start found; it is not in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list) and no Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows about 93% of its footprint within the much larger active lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln, about 15,900 sq m, recorded 2024-10-15). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to real street positions at multiple points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows most of this footprint within the much larger active lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln), not a lot of its own.
properties.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D shows Block 5 (marked '5*', a potential district parking garage/grocery store site, like Blocks 1 and 13) with an 85 ft base and a 220 ft upper height (its colour-coded labels, '220'/85''); the '111'MAX' label sits on a tick-ended dimension line (a plan extent of the tower zone), not a height. Block 7's 240 ft is the tallest limit on the site. The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) permits Residential, Institutional, Retail, Non-Retail Sales/Services (office), Entertainment and limited PDR uses on Block 5 and not Laboratory or Life Science. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see the accuracy note for this shape. Status 'planned': shown in the final D4D, and SocketSite's October 2020 schedule table lists Block 5 in Phase 3 (vertical development 2031-2034). Use 'mixed': residential, institutional, retail, office and limited PDR uses are permitted (D4D Table 3.1.1).
